newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore investors sell U.S. stocks - paper.
newsitem.headline: Singapore investors sell U.S. stocks - paper.

text.p: Singapore based investors in United States equities took profit and divested US$2.1 billion in the third quarter of 1996 after making net purchases for five straight quarters, a report in the Singapore Business Times said on Tuesday.
The paper quoted Angela Cozzini, a global strategist with Cross Boarder Capital, a London-based global asset allocation research and advisory consultancy which complied the statistics.
Her data was culled from official U.S. sources including the Treasury, the Securities Industry Association and the Federal Reserve Board.
The largest Singapore investor is widely thought to be the Government of Singapore Investment Corporation (GIC), said the report.
The GIC manages Singapore's foreign reserves estimated at Singapore $100 billion.
With the divestment in the third quarter, Singapore based investors ended up with a net US$900 million worth of US equities.
Singapore was the single largest foreign seller of US stocks in that period followed by the Japanese, who sold a net US$1.3 billion, the report said.
The Singapore sales reversed its position as top foreign buyer of US stocks in the first half of 1996 when it bought US$3 billion worth of equities, said the paper.
